extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers, journal editors, and university administrators interested in peer-review reform (especially in economics and social sciences)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and procedural criteria for how academic peer review and journal certification should operate, and proposals for redesigning peer review (verification org, simultaneous submission, editorial teams, tenure reform). Geared toward systemic reforms rather than a single journal's instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals' three purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals serve three simultaneous purposes: (1) communication; (2) credentialing; and (3) archiving (the only purpose for which the journal was designed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this tripartite view to judge whether a journal's procedures are fit for purpose: communication is increasingly handled by pre-prints, universities handle credentialing, and journals' core designed function is archiving. Reforms should respect or reallocate these functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should not take years; the current process often takes months to years and creates long wait times and backlogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce serial resubmission delays, minimize reviewer queue length, and adopt processes (e.g., parallel submission or centralized verification) that materially shorten decision times. Timeliness is a key quality metric for the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of facts and contribution outside journals (TVO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of facts and assessment of contribution should take place outside the journal ecosystem via a parallel Verification Org (TVO) that automatically fact-checks and certifies manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TVO would require materials (code/data), run automated checks, generate a certification report, and distribute distributed human surveys; journals would require furnishing the TVO report as part of submission and could use it as a substitute for generalist referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require submission of code and data for empirical papers
rubrics_metrics.description: If it's an empirical paper, authors are required to submit code and data (if accessible) alongside the paper for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement enables automated fact-checking and allows independent verification; it should be a standard part of any pre-publication verification pipeline (modeled on RCT registries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated fact-checking and certification report
rubrics_metrics.description: TVO automatically fact-checks submissions and generates a certification report that journals can use during editorial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification report should be machine- and human-readable, include results of automated checks, and serve as an initial filter to reduce burden on journal reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed peer review via brief targeted surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute peer review by sending brief surveys to ~20 knowledgeable authors (invited because they are cited or should have been cited); surveys should take under 20 minutes and focus on specific passages or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys present title and abstract and ask focused questions like 'Does the cited claim in paragraph X hold up?' Aggregate results become part of the certification report; this guards against overgeneralized claims and citation omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of participation in distributed review
rubrics_metrics.description: The certification report should post who was invited to participate in distributed reviews and who actually participated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish invitation and participation lists alongside survey results so readers and editors can assess representativeness and potential biases in the distributed review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Git-like version history for manuscript verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be able to update submissions based on automated/distributed review feedback with changes logged in a git-like version history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an auditable trail of revisions and certification iterations so editors and readers can see how concerns were addressed over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design manuscripts to be machine/LLM-friendly
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers will need to be indexed differently so that they are 'LLM-friendly' and can have their insights correctly extracted; PDFs often strip structure and context and are not machine-consumable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt formats or metadata standards that preserve structure/context for automated readers (e.g., structured abstracts, semantic tagging) to reduce LLM overgeneralization and preserve nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submission to multiple journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow manuscripts to be simultaneously submitted to multiple journals instead of forcing serial submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel submission reduces wasted time, fosters competition among journals, and, when combined with centralized verification (TVO), mitigates duplicate reviewer effort by providing a shared certification report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized verification to reduce duplicate reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralizing verification through an organization like TVO resolves the tension that simultaneous submissions would waste referee time, because journals can rely on the shared certification rather than re-running the same basic checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a common verification artifact to prevent repetitive referee labor across journals and to ensure consistent baseline checks are performed once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace traditional ad-hoc reviewers with expanded journal editing teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Dispose of traditional reviewers and build out journal editing teams: move traditional referees into associate editor roles and expand the number of co-editors and associate editors to perform in-depth checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate editors act like reliable referees, perform thorough manuscript vetting, require revisions, and help curate submissions; this changes journals from certifiers to curators when paired with external verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI as first-pass reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Have AI serve as a first-pass reviewer (automated verification) before human editorial/associate-editor scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI can perform scalable checks to catch obvious issues and reduce load on human reviewers; human editors/AE's then focus on higher-level judgment and curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decisions should be more decisive given widened variance in quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Given AI-accelerated research will amplify variance from 'hollow slop' to novel contributions, editors must be more decisive about what to curate and publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should develop clearer standards for novelty and veracity and leverage verification outputs to make prompt, decisive judgments to handle increased submission volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform tenure and certification criteria away from journal prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities must change what counts as 'certification' for tenure so hiring and promotion do not rely primarily on journal prestige signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop alternative metrics and signals (e.g., verified contributions, open-source impact, certification reports, reproducible code/data) so that increased publishability doesn't trivialize tenure evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase transparency of referee reports and editorial correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence about the article (referee suggestions, editor decisions, manuscript modifications, number and identity of referees) is currently hidden; this opacity should be reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make referee reports and decision histories public (or at least accessible with certification) so readers can see the evolution of the manuscript and the substance of reviewer feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose conflicts of interest and limit editor-driven reviewer selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors can hand-pick reviewers and hence decide which 'peers' review a paper — a concern especially for politically charged topics; conflicts of interest are rarely reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require disclosure of reviewer-selection rationale and conflicts of interest, and implement safeguards to prevent strategic reviewer selection that biases review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report both veracity and novelty (e.g., a 'Rotten Tomatoes' score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification should include metrics for veracity of claims and novelty of contribution (possible aggregation into a simple score like Rotten Tomatoes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide standardized, easy-to-interpret summary metrics in the certification report, while retaining detailed evidence and survey results for nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage pre-registration and registries as a verification model
rubrics_metrics.description: Use existing models like RCT registries where journals and reviewers check compliance with pre-registered designs to inform verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand registry-style verification beyond RCTs where appropriate, and integrate registry checks into the certification pipeline for study design compliance and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect against diminishing marginal returns of multiple independent reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that many successive referee reports add little value (diminishing marginal product) and design review systems to avoid redundant reviewer labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use centralized certification and targeted distributed review to capture diverse perspectives without repeatedly soliciting similar basic checks from many generalist referees.
